summary: Satis Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University and taught at Presidency University.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta from around 1948 to 1955, and became the second director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested in 1999 and 2026).

Satoru Fujiwara works in the field of Buddhist studies. His posts include researcher at the Shinshu Otani-ha Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015) and lecturer at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Satoru Harada (born 1947) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (~1971–1973) and served as a research member at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978) and professor at Kokushikan University (~2000–2018).

Satoru Noriyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching positions at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2014) and later served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Bukkyo University (BA, MA, PhD) and the University of Michigan, he served as a professor (1996) and president (2014) at Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Satoshi Ito (born 1961) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 1989 and was appointed professor at Ibaraki University around 2005.
Satoshi Kono (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo and was appointed professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki is a scholar of archaeology, history, Buddhist studies, and Indology who completed a PhD at Kyoto University. He served as Assistant Professor at Kyoto University's Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).
Satya Narayan Goenka (1924–2013) was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin from around 1955 to 1971. In 1985, he founded the Vipassana Research Institute.

Satya Vrat Shastri (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist educated at the University of the Punjab and Banaras Hindu University. He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (1970–1995) and Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya (~1989–1991).

Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974) studied at Presidency University and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Calcutta and University of Dhaka, and served as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

Sayadaw U Pandita (1921–2016) was a Buddhist studies practitioner who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught meditation at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha from 1955, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw from 1982 to 1991, and founded and led the Paṇḍitārāma Meditation Center.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda (1927–2005) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Sayadaw U Paññāvanta. He served as Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (1999) and founder-abbot of Dhammānanda Vihara (~1993–2005).

Sayadaw U Thittila (1896–1997) studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University. In his Buddhist studies career, he served as a librarian at the Adyar Library and the Buddhist Society, and taught Buddhist philosophy at the University of Rangoon (1952).
Sayagyi U Ba Khin (1899–1971) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Saya Thet Gyi from around 1937 to 1945. He founded the International Meditation Centre.
Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under the supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi.
Sayori Tsubota is an Indology researcher who pursued doctoral studies at Osaka University (attested 2020) and served as a JSPS postdoctoral fellow (PD) at Tohoku University (attested 2026).
